source: Rent Restriction Act (Cap 296), Distress for Rent Act (Cap 293) & Small Claims Court Precedents
illegalActions: Locking the tenant's house or tampering with padlocks without a valid court decree
Disconnecting water, electricity, or essential amenities to enforce rent collection
Confiscating household items without proclamation by a licensed Court Auctioneer
Evicting tenants without issuing minimum statutory notice (typically 1 to 3 months)
Deducting standard wear-and-tear repainting costs from the tenant's deposit
lawfulDeductions: Documented rent or utility arrears unpaid at the date of vacating
Physical damage beyond normal wear and tear (broken tiles, damaged plumbing fixtures, hole in wall)
Failure to issue agreed contractual written notice prior to vacating
